headword: {女子中学生|じょしちゅうがくせい}
reading: じょしちゅうがくせい
gloss: female junior high school student; junior high school girl

definitions.gloss: a female student enrolled in junior high school (roughly ages 12–15 in Japan)
definitions.explanation: The standard, neutral term for a girl attending a Japanese {中学校|ちゅうがっこう} (junior high school, typically three years covering grades 7–9). The word is used in news reports, statistics, school announcements, and everyday conversation to specify the student's sex and school level at the same time.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{女子|じょし}→女子：03350_joshi⟧ (female, girl) + ⟦{中学生|ちゅうがくせい}→中学生：10973_chuugakusei⟧ (junior high school student). A straightforward compound that specifies both the sex and the school level of the student at once.

Japanese compulsory education runs through the end of junior high school, so a {女子中学生|じょしちゅうがくせい} is normally aged 12–15 (first-year 13, second-year 14, third-year 15, by academic-year reckoning).

REGISTER:
Neutral and commonly used in news articles, school notices, advertising, and academic writing. In casual conversation, speakers often drop ⟦{女子|じょし}→女子：03350_joshi⟧ and just say ⟦{中学生|ちゅうがくせい}→中学生：10973_chuugakusei⟧ if the sex is clear from context, or use more casual phrasing like ちゅうがく⟦{一|いち}{年生|ねんせい}→一年生：27559_ichinensei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{女|おんな}の{子|こ}→女の子：02865_onnanoko⟧.

NOTE ON USAGE:
Like its counterpart ⟦{女子高生|じょしこうせい}→女子高生：12381_joshikousei⟧, {女子中学生|じょしちゅうがくせい} appears frequently in crime-news headlines and in statistical reports that break figures down by sex and school level. It is a neutral descriptor, not a loaded term.
